newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-VETERAN EDDERY FAVOURITE FOR LEGER GLORY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-VETERAN EDDERY FAVOURITE FOR LEGER GLORY.

text.p: Pat Eddery, riding as well as ever at the age of 44, can add to his formidable tally with victory on the 3-1 favourite Dushyantor in Saturday's St Leger, the final classic of the English season.
The Irishman landed an astonishing five-timer at Haydock a week ago at cumulative odds of just under 11,000-1 and the jockeys' title is once again firmly in his grasp.
On Wednesday, the first day of the big four-day Doncaster festival, Eddery turned in a masterpiece.
Riding Eva Luna, a stablemate of Dushyantor's, in the St Leger equivalent for fillies, he dictated the pace to perfection and kept just enough up his sleeve to hold off some high-class opposition.
Saturday's partner Dushyantor was a gallant runner-up in the Epsom Derby to Shaamit, but disappointed when favourite in the Irish Derby, finishing a modest fourth.
However, he was back to his best in an important trial race at York last month and enjoys the confidence of 10-times champion trainer Henry Cecil.
"Some people seem to think the horse hasn't got a turn of foot (acceleration) but he quickened in the Derby and in his last race at York," Cecil said.
"I can only think that the Irish Derby might have come a bit too quickly for him. I thought he was well but I was wrong.
"Everyone says: `Will he stay?'. But I'm not worried at all. If I was a jockey I would ride him before everything else."
The Leger, at 14 1/2 furlongs (2.9 km), is a true test of stamina, and Eddery knows just what is required.
Second favourite Mons (4-1), trained by Luca Cumani, is ridden by young Spaniard Oscar Urbina, whose knowledge of Doncaster is condsiderably less than that of Eddery and Cecil.
But Urbina has caught the eye of late with some fine performances and Mons is not that far behind Dushyantor on their running at York.
Irish raider Gordi (6-1) has come in for considerable support, mainly on the strength of his Royal Ascot victory in June in the Queen's Vase.
Improving colt St Mawes (8-1), son of the Derby winner Shahrastani, finally got his act together last time out at Goodwood after disappointing in the Epsom Derby.
Champion jockey Frankie Dettori, who won last year's Leger on Classic Cliche, partners Shantou (8-1), who was third in the Derby, just behind Dushyantor.
He has chosen the colt ahead of Sharaf Kabeer (8-1), who races for the Godolphin operation. Sharaf Kabeer is another improving sort but on breeding may not stay the distance.
Clerkenwell (12-1) won the Ebor Handicap in fine style but it is rare for a handicapper to step up and win a classic.
Latest betting: 3-1 Dushyantor, 4-1 Mons, 6-1 Gordi, 8-1 Sharaf Kabeer, Shantou, St Mawes, 12-1 Clerkenwell, 14-1 and upwards others.
